name: Via Ferrata Fürenwand (Engelberg)
summary: An ultra-vertical, exposed alpine face climb requiring immense endurance. Features a dramatic wire ladder exit near the top with breathtaking views of Mount Titlis.

name: Via Ferrata Diavolo (Andermatt)
summary: A highly scenic, historic route tracking straight up through the rugged Schöllenen Gorge. Provides unique alpine vantage points directly over the iconic Devil's Bridge monuments.

name: Via Ferrata Jägihorn (Saas-Fee)
summary: The highest official via ferrata in the Western Alps, topping out at a staggering 3,206 meters. Highlights include an optional, adrenaline-pumping 4-cable suspension bridge.

name: Via Ferrata Daubenhorn (Leukerbad)
summary: The longest and toughest via ferrata in Switzerland. Carved directly into a massive 1,000-meter rock face, this route demands excellent physical conditioning and features a cave traverse.

name: Via Ferrata Braunwald (Glarus)
summary: A fantastic multi-stage route divided into three separate sections (ranging K3 to K5). Ideal for refining skills, it features a famous 40-meter suspension bridge.

name: Via Ferrata Mürren-Gimmelwald
summary: Unlike most routes, this one travels downwards along the sheer cliffs of the Lauterbrunnen Valley. Expect extreme exposure under your feet, zip lines, and a massive suspension bridge.

name: Via Ferrata Tichadigis (Andeer)
summary: Located deep within the Graubünden region, this technical route works up steep pine woodlands into highly exposed vertical slabs. Offers great, technical athletic movements.

name: Via Ferrata San Salvatore (Lugano)
summary: A short but crisp North-face workout tracking up Lugano's landmark mountain. Rewards climbers with uncompromised, panoramic, Mediterranean-style vistas over Lake Lugano.

name: Via Ferrata de la Face (Verbier)
summary: A challenging modern route containing athletic overhanging sections, minimal natural footholds, and intense physical arm pump. Designed strictly for seasoned mountain veterans.

name: Via Ferrata Gabi Simpson (Simplon)
summary: A lower-altitude route navigating along the historic Simplon Pass cliffs. A great introductory climb with steady foot placements, beautiful gorge views, and minimal sustained fatigue.

name: Via Ferrata Moléson (Fribourg)
summary: Ascends the bold North face of Le Moléson peak. Features very steady cables but steep, vertical dropoffs that test your head for heights. Finishes right at a panoramic summit restaurant.

name: Via Ferrata Brunni Schonegg (Engelberg)
summary: Perfect beginner-friendly alpine itinerary located directly opposite the Fürenwand. Highly secure, well-stepped with steel rungs, and incredibly family-friendly.

name: Via Ferrata ViaFarinetta / ßFarinet Gorge (Saillon)
summary: Divided into progressive sectors traveling deep inside a narrow river canyon. The final optional overhang section is famously intense, passing directly beneath a historic footbridge.

name: Via Ferrata Allmenalp (Kandersteg)
summary: One of Switzerland's most creative routes, ascending a thundering 350-meter waterfall. Includes unique features like a high-wire Nepalese bridge and turning ladders.

name: Via Ferrata Rigidalstock (Engelberg)
summary: An excellent mid-tier mountain route combining traditional alpine ridge walking with vertical, cabled crag scaling. Climbs directly to a rewarding summit cross at 2,593m.

name: Via Ferrata Gemsstock (Andermatt)
summary: High alpine ridge route reaching nearly 3,000m. Highly exposed scramble over sharp granite teeth requiring cold-weather alpine experience and excellent footwork.

name: Via Ferrata Tälli (Meiringen)
summary: The pioneer of Swiss via ferratas. A massive, classical alpine wall traverse across the Gadmen Valley, heavily secured with ladders across natural ledge systems.

name: Via Ferrata Tierbergli (Susten Pass)
summary: An exquisite high-alpine route ending at the Tierbergli alpine hut. Climbs through smooth glacier-carved granite slabs right alongside active ice falls.

name: Via Ferrata Schwarzhorn (Grindelwald)
summary: Accessible via the First cable car, this long alpine ridge climb features steep iron ladders culminating in panoramic views over the Eiger, Mönch, and Jungfrau peaks.

name: Via Ferrata Eiger Rotstock
summary: Climb right on the edge of the world's most famous rock face. This historic, medium-difficulty route puts you directly on the flank of the legendary Eiger North Face.

name: Via Ferrata Kandersteg-Oeschinensee
summary: A gorge-based climb routing along a rushing glacial stream from the iconic Oeschinensee lake. Moderate steepness makes it a highly scenic intermediate option.

name: Via Ferrata Nax (Espace Mont-Noble)
summary: The via ferrata of the 'Belvédère'. Offering absolute verticality but plenty of iron rungs, it yields an expansive, clear view over the Rhone Valley layout.

name: Via Ferrata Mauvoisin Gorge
summary: Split into two segments (Saxifrage and Tichodrome). It tracks through a spectacular deep gorge directly under the massive, towering Mauvoisin concrete dam wall.

name: Via Ferrata Evolène
summary: A physically punishing, highly athletic route with several severely overhanging sections. Demands great upper-body strength and dynamic cable-clipping technique.

name: Via Ferrata Aletsch (Gibidum Dam)
summary: Looping completely around the Gibidum reservoir canyon at the foot of the Great Aletsch Glacier. Famous for its long, bouncy 80-meter Nepalese suspension bridge.

name: Via Ferrata Gornergrat (Zermatt)
summary: A striking modern panorama route facing the iconic pyramid peak of the Matterhorn. Blends steep, technical vertical columns with exceptional mountain geometry.

name: Via Ferrata Belalp-Riederalp
summary: A scenic canyon traverse across the Massa Gorge. Requires careful stepping along rocky ledges and spans a massive suspension bridge over active white-water flows.

name: Via Ferrata Pinut (Flims)
summary: The oldest documented via ferrata in Switzerland (renovated). A historic, incredibly gentle route ascending natural terraces and caves. Ideal for absolute beginners.

name: Via Ferrata Greina (Piz da la Margna)
summary: A remote, high-altitude route tracing along the edges of the wild Greina Plateau. Offers isolation, rolling panoramic views, and a traditional alpine landscape experience.
